explanation: The pole is a retrospective letter-w detector on the token it sits on: it fires when the measured token begins with w/W — short word-initial fragments and name pieces (' Wa', ' Wil', ' Wal', ' W', 'WH', 'wh', 'wi', the strongest of all), the written w of ordinary words ('whole', 'wolf', 'wing'; weaker but usually over the active line), and the w-letter of other scripts (kana 'ワーク'/'ワ'/'ヲ', which fires as strongly) — and the same response lands on the next token when a w ends a preceding word fragment ('ew'->'a' in Swahili, '-w'->'he' in 'two-wheeled'). It falls to the noise floor when the same slot carries the same word under any other initial letter ('Val' for 'Wal', 'golf' for 'wolf', 'short' for 'whole', 'groei' for 'werking' in Dutch), when the w sits inside the token ('answer', 'swim', 'between'), and it is weakest on the highest-frequency w-function words of running English ('was', 'with', 'will').
